11	/-!
12	# Affine tensor-section substrate (`TensorSectionFormula`)
13	
14	This file collects the substrate for the affine tensor-section
15	formula that feeds the quasi-coherent case of
16	`Scheme.Modules.pullbackTensorMap_isIso` ([Stacks 01CD]; the section formula is
17	[Stacks 01CD]/[Stacks 01CA] read on a basis of affine opens).
18	
19	For `A B : X.Modules` the substrate tensor `Scheme.Modules.tensorObj A B`
20	(`Picard/TensorObjSubstrate.lean`) is the sheafification of the presheaf-of-modules
21	tensor `P := PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj A.val B.val` of the underlying
22	presheaves.  Objectwise, `P(V) = Γ(A, V) ⊗_{Γ(X, V)} Γ(B, V)`
23	(`tensorPresheaf_obj`), so the sheafification unit provides a canonical
24	`Γ(X, V)`-linear **section comparison**
25	
26	  `tensorSectionHom A B V : Γ(A, V) ⊗_{Γ(X, V)} Γ(B, V) ⟶ Γ(tensorObj A B, V)`
27	
28	for every open `V` (`tensorSectionHom`), natural in restriction
29	(`tensorSectionHom_naturality_apply`).  Over the total space it is exactly the
30	section multiplication `sectionsMul` of the graded-ring machinery
31	(`tensorSectionHom_top_eq_sectionsMul`), and the substrate `tensorObj` and the
32	section-graded `sheafTensorObj` are the same object
33	(`tensorObjIsoSheafTensorObj`, definitional).
34	
35	## Contents
36	
37	* `tensorPresheaf` — the presheaf-of-modules tensor of the underlying presheaves.
38	* `tensorSectionHom` — the section comparison map at an open `V`.
39	* `tensorPresheaf_obj` — the objectwise identification of the domain as
40	  `Γ(A, V) ⊗ Γ(B, V)`.
41	* `tensorSectionHom_naturality_apply` — restriction naturality.
42	* `tensorSectionHom_top_eq_sectionsMul` — the `⊤`-value is `sectionsMul`.
43	* `tensorObjIsoSheafTensorObj` — the (definitional) `tensorObj ≅ sheafTensorObj`
44	  bridge.
45	* `isIso_sheafification_tensorSectionUnit` — the categorical crux: sheafifying the
46	  presheaf comparison unit is an isomorphism (the reflective localization inverts
47	  the unit), which is why the affine formula reduces to the presheaf-tensor
48	  localization on a basis of affine opens.
49	
50	## Remaining obligations (the quasi-coherent case of `pullbackTensorMap_isIso`)
51	
52	The genuinely hard step — promoting `tensorSectionHom A B V` to a `LinearEquiv`
53	for quasi-coherent `A B` and *affine* `V` — is not carried out here: it requires
54	computing the sheafification value on the basis of basic opens as a localization
55	of the presheaf tensor, against the (currently `private`) tilde-comparison engine
56	of `Picard/QuotScheme.lean`.  Concretely, it remains to:
57	
58	1. On a basic open `D(f) ⊆ V` (affine `V = Spec Γ(X, V)`), identify
59	   `Γ(A, D(f)) = Γ(A, V)_f` and `Γ(B, D(f)) = Γ(B, V)_f` via
60	   `isLocalizedModule_basicOpen_of_isQuasicoherent` (QuotScheme.lean), so
61	   `P(D(f)) = Γ(A, V)_f ⊗_{Γ(X, V)_f} Γ(B, V)_f`.
62	2. Feed `LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct` /
63	   `RingTheory.Localization.BaseChange` to identify this with
64	   `(Γ(A, V) ⊗_{Γ(X, V)} Γ(B, V))_f`, i.e. `P` is a localizing presheaf on the
65	   basic-open basis; hence `tensorObj A B|_V` is the tilde of
66	   `Γ(A, V) ⊗ Γ(B, V)` and `tensorSectionHom A B V` is a `LinearEquiv`.
67	3. Transport through `Modules.pullback_app_isoTensor` (QuotScheme.lean, the
68	   pullback side) and globalize by `isIso_of_isIso_restrict` over the affine cover,
69	   discharging the `pullbackTensorMap_restrict` restriction coherence.
70	
71	### On the generality of `pullbackTensorMap_isIso`
72	
73	`Modules.pullbackTensorMap_isIso` is stated for *arbitrary* `A B` (no
74	quasi-coherence hypothesis), matching the general [Stacks 01CD] statement for
75	ringed spaces, whereas the chart chase above only closes the *quasi-coherent*
76	case.  Its sole consumer (`pullback_moduleTensorPow_iso`) already carries
77	`[F.IsQuasicoherent] [L.IsQuasicoherent]`, so a quasi-coherent variant assuming
78	`[A.IsQuasicoherent] [B.IsQuasicoherent]` would be enough for that consumer and
79	would avoid the general ringed-space stalk machinery.
80	-/

    11	
    12	This file constructs the **étale-sheafified relative Picard functor**
    13	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}` of a smooth proper curve `C/k` and proves that it *is* a sheaf
    14	for the étale topology — the object whose representability is the project's
    15	central open obligation (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).
    16	
    17	## Why the sheafification is the right object
    18	
    19	The relative Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
    20	(`Scheme.PicSharp.relPresheaf`, Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`) is in general **not
    21	a sheaf**, not even for the Zariski topology (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302): a line
    22	bundle on `C ×_k T` can be trivial on each member of a cover of `T` without
    23	being trivial modulo `π_T^* Pic(T)`, because the gluing data is a `Pic`-class
    24	of the overlaps. Kleiman's representability theorem (§4 Thm. `th:main`) is
    25	therefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that
    26	statement which is true over an arbitrary base field with no rational-point
    27	hypothesis.
    28	
    29	There are two ways to reach a sheaf, and they differ in what has to be
    30	supplied:
    31	
    32	1. assume `C` has a `k`-rational point. Then Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 says the
    33	   comparison `Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is already bijective, so the plain
    34	   presheaf is the sheaf. This is *strictly weaker* than the challenge, whose
    35	   curve need not have a rational point, and it is the route the conditional
    36	   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;
    37	2. sheafify. Nothing is assumed about `C(k)`, and the sheaf axiom holds by
    38	   construction. This is the route realised here and the one the project
    39	   claims (owner decision of 2026-07-28).
    40	
    41	## The site
    42	
    43	Mathlib `v4.31` carries the big étale site on schemes,
    44	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology = grothendieckTopology @Etale`
    45	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`). The relative Picard presheaf
    46	lives on the slice `Over (Spec k)` rather than on `Scheme`, so the topology is
    47	transported along the localisation of SGA 4 III 5.2.1, available in Mathlib as
    48	`GrothendieckTopology.over`: a sieve of `T : Over (Spec k)` covers iff the
    49	corresponding sieve of `T.left` covers étale-locally. That transport is where
    50	"the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`" becomes a definition rather than a parameter,
    51	and it is what lets the sheaf property below be a *theorem* rather than a
    52	hypothesis.
    53	
    54	## Main definitions

    56	* `Scheme.etaleTopologyOver k` — the étale topology on `(Sch/k) = Over (Spec k)`.

    59	  relative Picard presheaf.

    61	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    62	    Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
    63	  (CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}).obj

    69	for the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`. This is `Sheaf.cond` of the bundled

    73	subcanonical topology, so a non-sheaf can never be representable — which is
    74	exactly why the unsheafified `relPresheaf` needs a rational point).

    83	sheafification adjunction at the relative Picard presheaf.
    84	
    85	Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`) says this map is an isomorphism when `C` has a
    86	`k`-rational point (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic here). Over an
    87	arbitrary base field it is only a comparison: the honest object is the target,
    88	which is why the representability obligation is stated there. -/

    91	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
    92	  CategoryTheory.toSheafify (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianData
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0SigmaSheaf
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Producing the Jacobian representability datum from a Zariski chart family
    11	
    12	The pinned datum `JacobianData C` of the curve `C` bundles a representing object for the
    13	degree-zero Picard functor together with the two finiteness certificates of that object.
    14	This file constructs it: first from a bare representation (`JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy`),
    15	and then — the substance — from a Zariski chart family of the Σ-extension sheaf, whose glued
    16	scheme is the representing object and whose charts carry the finiteness.
    17	
    18	## Main declarations
    19	
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy` — a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C`
    21	  by `J`, plus `LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom` and `QuasiCompact J.hom`, is a `JacobianData C`.
    22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedHom` / `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedOfCharts` — the glued scheme of a chart
    23	  family, placed over the base field by the Σ-component of the universal element of the
    24	  representation it induces.
    25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom` — the structure morphism `X i ⟶ Spec k` of the `i`-th chart:
    26	  the Σ-component of the element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.toGlued_comp_gluedHom` — **the compatibility of the two**: the glue map
    28	  `X i ⟶ gluedOfCharts` composed with the structure morphism of the glued object is exactly
    29	  `chartHom i`.  So the charts are charts *over the base field*, and the glued object is
    30	  covered by them as a `k`-scheme.
    31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` — being locally of finite type is local
    32	  on the source, so it descends from the charts to the glued object.
    33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_gluedHom` — over the affine base `Spec k`, quasi-compactness
    34	  of the glued object is compactness of its space, which a finite family of compact charts
    35	  supplies.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofCharts` — **the first producer of the Jacobian datum**:
    37	  a finite Zariski chart family of relatively representable open immersions into
    38	  `pic0SigmaSheaf C`, jointly locally surjective, with quasi-compact charts that are locally of
    39	  finite type over `k`, yields `JacobianData C`.
    40	
    41	## The hypothesis bundle
    42	
    43	Every declaration here carries exactly the three hypotheses of the frozen `Jacobian` of
    44	`Challenge.lean` — `IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  The
    45	`GeometricallyReduced C.hom` hypothesis of `Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` is *not* an extra assumption:
    46	a morphism smooth of relative dimension `1` is smooth (`Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one`)
    47	and a smooth morphism is geometrically reduced (`Smooth.geometricallyReduced`), both global
    48	instances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, so instance resolution supplies it
    49	from the frozen bundle.  The `example` at the end of this file is the machine-checked record.
    50	-/

    53	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

    62	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]

    65	/-! ## Packaging a representation as the datum -/

    67	/-- **Package a representation of the degree-zero Picard functor**, with its two finiteness

    69	`pic0TypeFunctor` spelling; that abbreviation unfolds to the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage that

    72	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    73	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :
    74	    JacobianData C where

    76	  rep := rep

    84	    (JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft hqc).J = J :=

    90	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom) :

    94	/-- The universal property of a packaged datum is the packaged representation. -/

    96	lemma JacobianData.homEquiv_ofRepresentableBy (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    97	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    98	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom) (hqc : QuasiCompact J.hom)
    99	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (g : T ⟶ J) :

    (V : Y.AffineCoverMVSquare) (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom f] :
    X.AffineCoverMVSquare where
  U₁ := f ⁻¹ᵁ V.U₁
  U₂ := f ⁻¹ᵁ V.U₂
  isAffineOpen_U₁ := V.isAffineOpen_U₁.preimage f
  isAffineOpen_U₂ := V.isAffineOpen_U₂.preimage f
  isAffineOpen_inf := V.isAffineOpen_inf.preimage f
  cover := by
    change f ⁻¹ᵁ (V.U₁ ⊔ V.U₂) = ⊤
    rw [V.cover]
    rfl

/-! ## §2. Fibrewise `h⁰` and `h¹`-vanishing for a family -/

/-- The **fibrewise `h⁰`** of a sheaf of modules `L` on the total space of a
family `q : X ⟶ S` at a point `t : S`: the dimension over the residue field
`κ(t)` of the global sections of the restriction `L_t` of `L` to the
scheme-theoretic fibre `X_t = q.fiber t`,

`h⁰(t) = dim_{κ(t)} Γ(X_t, L_t)`.

The `κ(t)`-structure is `Scheme.Hom.fiberSectionsModule` (restriction of
scalars along `κ(t) → Γ(X_t, 𝒪)`), exactly the convention of
`Scheme.hilbertFunction`; when the dimension is infinite, `Module.finrank`
takes the junk value `0`.  This is the (P2-kit-independent) fibre `h⁰`
vocabulary of campaign milestones B3/B5/B6/J1/J3. -/
noncomputable def Hom.fiberH0 (q : X ⟶ S) (L : X.Modules) (t : S) : ℕ :=
  letI := q.fiberSectionsModule t (q.fiberModule t L)
  Module.finrank (S.residueField t) Γ(q.fiberModule t L, (⊤ : (q.fiber t).Opens))

/-- **Fibrewise `h¹`-vanishing** of a sheaf of modules `L` on the total space
of a family `q : X ⟶ S` at a point `t : S`, in the weakest honest form the
adelic lane can express before the P2 cohomology kit exists: *some* 2-affine
Čech cover of the scheme-theoretic fibre `X_t = q.fiber t` has surjective
difference-of-restrictions map for `L_t` — equivalently (by
`AffineCoverMVSquare.subsingleton_moduleH1Cok_iff`) vanishing concrete Čech
`Ȟ¹(𝒰, L_t)`.

On the separated fibre curves of the campaign this Čech `Ȟ¹` computes sheaf
`H¹(X_t, L_t)` and is independent of the chosen 2-affine cover
(Mayer–Vietoris); the ∃-form is implied by every future P2-kit form of
`h¹ = 0`, so hypotheses pinned this way only get easier to supply.
Cover-independence Čech-to-Čech is the recorded **P2-interface TODO**. -/
def Hom.FiberH1Vanishing (q : X ⟶ S) (L : X.Modules) (t : S) : Prop :=
  ∃ V : (q.fiber t).AffineCoverMVSquare,
    Function.Surjective ⇑(V.moduleSectionDiff (q.fiberModule t L))
